author: Maya Yang
description:
Republican Greg Abbott says datacenters must help ‘protect’ drought-prone state and disclose water use

Greg Abbott, the Texas governor, has directed state regulators to penalize datacenters that fail to comply with state laws requiring them to disclose their water use.

“Data centers must share the duty to protect Texas water,” the Republican governor said on Monday. “The Texas Water Code requires a complete and accurate water use survey. I direct the Texas Water Development Board to use its enforcement authority to penalize past failures and to impose legal consequences for any future failure to comply,” he adde
title: Texas governor threatens to penalize datacenters not obeying water laws

author: Sam Levine in New York
description:
Officers were instructed to search state voter databases and create federal records on suspected non-citizen voters despite concerns over the process

Department of Homeland Security (DHS) lawyers told officers investigating voter fraud they would not be held responsible for violating state laws around accessing voter registration information, an anonymous whistleblower revealed on Monday. DHS officers also had concerns about the reliability of the data they were working with, the whistleblower said.

The Trump administration has ramped up its investigation into noncitizen voting ahead of the midterm elections. Noncitizen voting is extremely rare and the effort has only turned up a handful of cases so f
title: DHS officers raise concerns over potentially illegal voter searches and unreliable data, whistleblower says

author: Guardian Staff
description:
Committee to reconsider Harry and Meghan’s publicly funded police protection now they are full-time residents

The Duke and Duchess of Sussex will have a review of their publicly funded security following their return to the UK.

Ravec (Royal and VIP Executive Committee), which oversees tax-funded security for royalty and public figures, is to reconsider Harry and Meghan’s level of police protection.

Continue reading...
title: Duke and Duchess of Sussex granted security review after return to UK

author: Chris Stein
description:
The 84-year-old said he was prepared to cast his first vote after rampant speculation about his health

Mitch McConnell, the former Republican Senate majority leader, returned to the Capitol on Monday and cast his first vote after a months‑long absence that fueled rampant speculation about his health.

The 84-year-old senator has been away from the Senate since mid-June, following what his office said was a fall that left him hospitalized. He was discharged from a rehabilitation center last month.

Continue reading...
title: Mitch McConnell returns to Senate after months-long absence

author: Martin Farrer
description:
Follow the day’s news live

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Good morning and welcome to our live news blog. I’m Martin Farrer with the top overnight stories and then it will be Krishani Dhanji with the main action.

Let’s begin.

Continue reading...
title: Australia politics live: Hastie accuses Hanson of avoiding media; Anthony Albanese and King Charles speak

author: Melody Schreiber
description:
CDC announces changes to how it reports measles deaths as Pennsylvania continues to confirm more cases

The Trump administration has changed the way it counts measles deaths amid an outbreak in Pennsylvania, which on Sunday saw the third apparent measles-related death in the state reported by a local coroner.

The US Centers for Disease Control and Prevention (CDC) is now using data from the National Center for Health Statistics (NCHS), which is a way to track mortality trends over time, according to a note published to the agency’s website on 4 September.

Continue reading...
title: Trump administration changes how it counts measles deaths amid Pennsylvania outbreak

author: Pippa Crerar, Jessica Elgot and Kiran Stacey
description:
Plans to strengthen legislation already going through parliament might mean donors having to meet stricter UK residence requirements

Andy Burnham’s government could thwart Reform’s unprecedented £72m donations with retrospective restrictions on political donors that will include tough new residency requirements, ministers have announced.

In a move that is likely to set off furious complaints from Nigel Farage’s party, the government will table amendments to legislation going through the House of Lords within weeks that puts the legality of Reform’s latest donations in doubt.

Continue reading...
title: Amendment to bill in Lords could test legality of £72m Reform donations

author: Roque Planas
description:
Cal Fire official says Sunday was ‘big turning point’ to reduce blaze in Lake county, now 30% contained

Firefighters made progress toward containing northern California’s Lucas fire, state officials said on Sunday.

Fire officials are still investigating the cause of the fire, which has burned more than 4,120 acres across Lake and Mendocino counties. The fire was 30% contained by Monday morning, according to the California department of forestry and fire protection, or Cal Fire.

Continue reading...
title: Firefighters make progress to contain northern California’s Lucas fire

author: Alice Speri
description:
Lawsuit accuses university of ‘deliberate indifference’ and failure to respond to ‘persistent and coordinated harassment’

Mahmoud Khalil announced on Monday that he’s sued Columbia University, accusing the New York City school he attended of a years-long history of anti-Palestinian discrimination, indifference to harassment, and retaliation.

Khalil, a US green card holder of Palestinian descent, was a graduate student at Columbia’s School of International and Public Affairs (SIPA) when he was arrested at his university apartment by federal immigration agents in March 2025, the first of a number of foreign nationals that the Trump administration has detained and sought to deport over their pro-Palestinian advocacy.
title: Mahmoud Khalil sues Columbia University over years of alleged anti-Palestinian discrimination

author: Dan Milmo and agency
description:
Central bank chief says continent’s AI dependency could give trade partners unprecedented leverage in negotiations

Europe must develop its own AI technology and build more datacentres in order to nullify the threat of being cut off by the US or China, according to the president of the European Central Bank.

Christine Lagarde said the continent needed AI models – the technology that powers AI tools such as chatbots – that were “good enough” to carry out most tasks and run from domestic datacentres. If Europe invests in its own AI tech, said Lagarde, “the threat of being cut off loses its force”.

Continue reading...
title: Europe must build own AI or risk getting cut off by US or China, says ECB’s Lagarde

author: Adria R Walker
description:
The policy allows immigration officers the authority to deny green cards to those using public benefits

A coalition of 22 states and the District of Columbia sued the Trump administration on Monday over a new policy that would allow individual immigration officers to deny green cards based on use of public benefits.

The new policy changes a long-established “public charge” rule, which dates back to the Immigration Act of 1882, established to ensure that newcomers to the country would be able to provide for themselves without relying on governmental benefits.

Continue reading...
title: States and cities sue Trump administration over policy restricting green card benefits

author: Edward Helmore
description:
Firm publishes AI guidelines with Microsoft AI CEO saying: ‘AI must be subordinate and always in service of people’

Microsoft published a provisional “code of conduct” Monday to apply to the training of new artificial intelligence models, taking a step towards limiting the capabilities of the company’s AI as anxiety rises over the prospect that technology companies could lose control of AI products.

Mustafa Suleyman, the CEO of Microsoft AI, published the code on social media early Monday, writing: “AI must be subordinate and always in service of people.

Continue reading...
title: Microsoft proposes limits on its AI with code of conduct amid safety debate

author: Lucy Campbell
description:
US president’s eldest child married Palm Beach socialite Bettina Anderson in three-day celebration across two exclusive private islands

  • US politics live – latest updates

A top Democrat has demanded answers after it was reported that a Russian oligarch close to Vladimir Putin paid hundreds of thousands of dollars toward Donald Trump Jr’s wedding in the Bahamas earlier this year.

Trump Jr, the US president’s eldest child, married Palm Beach socialite Bettina Anderson in a lavish three-day celebration across two exclusive private islands in May, which according to ProPublica was partially bankrolled by Umar Kremlev, a member of the Russian president’s circle.
title: Russian oligarch close to Putin reportedly paid for part of Donald Trump Jr’s lavish wedding

author: Maya Yang
description:
Teen was swimming at a popular spot at the time of the attack, the latest in a string that have occurred in the state

A 13-year-old Maryland boy is reported to be recovering from multiple surgeries and nerve damage after being attacked by a rabid beaver.

The teen, Dominick Cebula, was swimming at a popular spot in Cunningham Falls state park in Thurmont, Maryland, on 26 July when a beaver attacked his chest underwater, a relatively rare kind of encounter that more recently has been recurring, according to reporting from local news outlets.

Continue reading...
title: Maryland boy recovering from surgeries after rabid beaver attack at state park

author: Associated Press
description:
Subpoena is among a flurry issued in recent weeks as part of DoJ inquiry into alleged conspiracy against Trump

The former CIA director John Brennan has been subpoenaed to testify next month before a Florida grand jury as part of a Department of Justice investigation into whether former law enforcement and intelligence officials conspired against Donald Trump, one of his lawyers said Monday.

Ken Wainstein, an attorney for Brennan, disclosed in a court filing that prosecutors last Thursday presented him with a subpoena for Brennan to appear before a grand jury in Fort Pierce, Florida, on 15 October.

Continue reading...
title: Ex-CIA director John Brennan subpoenaed in Trump ‘grand conspiracy’ investigation

author: Rachel Leingang
description:
Congresswoman awarded the convicted abuser and musician a congressional record recognition in Arlington

Democratic US representative Jasmine Crockett is under fire for honoring musician Chris Brown, a convicted abuser, with an official recognition at a Texas concert over the weekend.

Crockett, a Texas congresswoman, awarded Brown and R&B musician Usher a congressional record recognition at a performance in Arlington, Texas, on Saturday. Appearing alongside Texas state representative Venton Jones, Crockett said she was there to “honor” Brown and Usher.

Continue reading...
title: Texas Democrat Jasmine Crockett under fire for honoring Chris Brown at concert

author: PA media
description:
Ministry of Defence says person died in road incident understood not to be result of hostile action

A member of the UK armed forces has been killed in a crash in Ukraine, the Ministry of Defence (MoD) said.

The MoD said the person died in a road traffic incident on Saturday.

Continue reading...
title: UK armed forces member killed in crash in Ukraine

author: Petra Stock
description:
Batteries now meet almost half of the grid’s dispatchable power needs during hours of highest demand

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Australia’s dependence on gas for power during the evening, when the grid is under the most pressure, has fallen by almost nearly 70% over the past year as batteries surged in, replacing the fossil fuel.

Gas generation during the busy early evening, between 5pm and 8pm, fell by 67% in the year to August, as large-scale batteries continued to come online and half a million
title: Australia’s dependence on gas generation during evening energy peak falls by almost 70%

author: Jack Larkin
description:
Rainbow clouds are not uncommon in Australia but rarely photographed, and experts say they get their colours when light is diffracted around ice crystals

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Rainbow clouds shone over parts of Victoria over the weekend, in an unusual visual phenomenon known as iridescent clouds.

Photographs of the spectacle were taken by onlookers in the Melbourne suburbs of Mount Waverley and Caroline Springs.
title: Cloudy with a chance of rainbow: iridescent clouds brighten the sky over parts of Victoria

author: Achol Arok
description:
Newly collated data also shows Indigenous Australians experiencing disproportionally high rates of infection

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Rates of reported gonorrhoea and infectious syphilis have increased by more than 50% across Australia over the past decade, with experts warning of concerning rises among women.

Newly collated sexual health data from UNSW’s Kirby Institute shows 42,393 gonorrhoea notifications and 5,986 infectious syphilis notifications were recorded in 2025. The figures represent 10-year increases of 57% and 56%, respectively.
title: Gonorrhoea and syphilis rise by more than 50% in Australia with ‘concerning’ rise in cases in women

author: Andrew Messenger
description:
Exclusive: Advocate says homeless clearances should be halted after man is hospitalised during confrontation in Brisbane park

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

A homeless man was shot with a Taser by police after attempting to take his own life during a tent city clearance, sparking calls for mental health considerations when dealing with move-on orders amid Queensland’s homelessness crisis.

On 1 September, Moreton Bay city council rangers gave six homeless residents 24 hours to leave Pelican Park north of Brisbane, where Martin* had been living in a camper trailer, to make way for a kite festival this weekend.
title: Queensland homeless man shot with Taser after being given move-on order to make way for kite festival

author: Sarah Martin Senior correspondent
description:
Pauline Hanson’s gas policy and the party’s relationship with Rinehart is examined in a new Guardian podcast series, The Populist

  • Listen: The Populist: Aeroplanes and bulldozers | Episode 1 – podcast

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

One Nation has come under fire for quietly shelving support for a new domestic gas reservation policy in preference for a policy that favours the party’s billionaire patron, Gina Rinehart.

The Albanese government has announced
title: One Nation under fire for abandoning gas reservation plan in favour of policy benefiting Gina Rinehart

author: Josh Halliday North of England editor
description:
Some of the arguments inconsistent with ‘available evidence, science and established physiology’, say pair

Two leading experts have withdrawn from Lucy Letby’s defence team over concerns about the “scientific credibility” of some of its evidence.

The former neonatal nurse is challenging her convictions for murdering seven babies and attempting to murder seven others at the Countess of Chester hospital in north-west England.

Continue reading...
title: Experts quit Lucy Letby’s defence team over ‘scientific credibility’ concerns

author: Ramon Antonio Vargas
description:
Woman, her daughter, her son and his girlfriend identified as victims in incident that also critically wounded a child

A Louisiana woman, her daughter, her son and his girlfriend have been identified as the four victims killed in a stabbing spree on Saturday that also left a young child critically wounded in the southern part of the state, according to a relative and family advocate.

Verna Mae Verdin, her daughter Letha Verrett, her son Paul Verret, and his girlfriend Krissy Lynn Parfait were stabbed to death at their home in the community of Houma, the relative and advocate, Brandon Thiel, told Louisiana television news station WVUE and said on an online campaign raising funds in part for the victims’ funeral expenses.
title: Four victims identified in Louisiana stabbing spree after suspect detained

author: Peter Walker Senior political correspondent
description:
Prime minister had been due to speak at the TUC conference in Brighton

  • UK politics live – latest updates

Andy Burnham has cancelled his engagements for Monday and Tuesday after his father, Roy, died.

Among other plans, the prime minister had been due to speak to the TUC conference in Brighton on Tuesday.

Continue reading...
title: Andy Burnham cancels engagements as his father’s death is announced

author: Eromo Egbejule in Abidjan and agencies
description:
Public offering of Aliko Dangote’s Nigerian oil refinery business could swell his net wealth by two thirds

The fortune of Africa’s richest person could swell by two thirds to nearly $60bn (£44bn) after his refinery in Nigeria listed publicly in the continent’s biggest-ever initial public offering.

If Monday’s flotation of Dangote Petroleum Refinery and Petrochemicals goes to plan, then Aliko Dangote will add another $23bn (£17bn) to his $35bn net worth.

Continue reading...
title: Africa’s richest man aiming to make $23bn from continent’s biggest-ever IPO

author: Jessica Elgot and Peter Walker
description:
Sources say there are ‘significant differences’ in opinion as debate inflamed by crypto billionaires’ £72m donations to Reform

  • UK politics live – latest updates

The head of Britain’s trade union movement, Paul Nowak, has said the government must act to “stop the super-rich corrupting our politics”, as union leaders met on Monday to discuss possible support for a domestic cap on donations.

Union leaders are split on the prospect of limiting domestic donations to political parties, with many including the GMB fearing it would lead a future rightwing government to curb union donations.
title: UK unions split over donations cap as TUC chief says ‘super-rich’ corrupting politics

author: Martin Belam
description:
Strike on kingdom’s east-west pipeline could affect 4% of global oil supply. Plus, report reveals British monarchy’s role in financing slave trade

Good morning. Oil prices have climbed above $108 a barrel after a series of drone attacks from Iraq’s territory forced Saudi Arabia to close its east-west crude pipeline. Saudi traders said the kingdom would run out of oil stocks for export if it did not reopen within days. Gas prices also climbed higher. Energy prices have surged this year, as the US-Israel war with Iran has disrupted oil and gas supply across the Middle East.

The spike came as the Iran-aligned Houthi forces in Yemen launched several attacks against Saudi Arabia and captured the strategic island of Perim in the Bab al-Mandab strait on Sunday, expanding their control of the waterway.

Where did the attack on Saudi Arabia co
title: First Thing: Oil prices surge as attacks on Saudi Arabia stoke supply fears

author: Dan Milmo and Robert Booth
description:
Warning follows series of safety incidents, with committee saying threats include public face-scanning and deepfakes

  • UK politics live – latest updates

British lawmakers are demanding more restrictions on the power of AI, warning the world is unprepared for the “potentially dire” consequences of the technology, in the latest sign of rising global concern.

A new regulatory framework is needed for AI in the UK, including an independent oversight body and legislation to protect the public, according to the cross-party joint committee on human rights, comprising MPs and Lords.

Continue reading...
title: UK MPs and Lords call for new laws to tackle AI threat to human rights

author: Emma Joyce
description:
STC’s 2027 program also features Celeste Barber in Amy Sedaris and David Sedaris play, Tim Minchin as Scrooge and the return of The Picture of Dorian Gray

Six years after the Australian historian Jenny Hocking won her legal battle to release secret correspondence between Queen Elizabeth II, Malcolm Fraser and the governor general John Kerr, her fight to reveal the truth about Gough Whitlam’s dismissal is being adapted for the stage.

The Palace Letters, announced on Monday as part of Sydney Theatre Company’s 2027 program, will have its world premiere at Sydney Opera House in April. It will star Georgie Parker as Hocking, with Jonathan Biggins playing Whitlam.

Continue reading...
title: Queen’s secret Whitlam correspondence inspires Sydney Theatre Company play in 2027

author: Andrew Sparrow
description:
Labour MPs and unions are pressuring the government to legislate for a stricter cap on political party donations

Good morning. This afternoon peers will debate the second reading of the representation of the people bill. If you hear a loud bang echo around the Lords chamber, it will be the sound of stable door being shut after the horse has bolted.

At the end of 2024 the Sunday Times carried a report saying that Elon Musk was considering donating $100m to Reform UK. It made a good headline, but the idea seemed so preposterous that no one at Westminster really took it very seriously. Musk is not a British citizen, and so it would have been illegal for him to have given the money directly anyway; he would have had to have donated via UK companies.

We’re completely confident that [the Delo and Harborne] donations comply with not only the existing rules, but they also comply with the rules currently going through parliament, albeit with that retrospective element …
title: Richard Tice accuses Labour of ‘trying to change rules retrospectively’ after Reform receive £72m in donations – UK politics live

author: Caitlin Cassidy
description:
Police in Bali believe the two young children died as a result of violence, while a 57-year-old man is believed to have taken his own life

Indonesian police are investigating the deaths of three Australians who died in Bali over the weekend, with initial reports suggesting a father killed his two young children before taking his own life.

The man, 57 and his two children, aged seven and four, who are also Indonesian citizens, were discovered deceased in a bungalow in Kuta on Sunday morning.

Continue reading...
title: Indonesian police investigate deaths of Australian man and two children in Bali as suspected murder-suicide

author: Lauren Almeida
description:
Shares in tech firms tumble across Asia with Nasdaq also likely to dip later after Anthropic, OpenAI and SpaceX leaders back call

  • Business news – live updates

AI-linked stocks tumbled on Monday after the bosses of Anthropic, OpenAI and SpaceX called for a slowdown in “reckless” development citing fears the technology could soon run out of control.

Shares in SoftBank, a Japanese investor that is a big backer of OpenAI, slumped 13%, while the South Korean Kospi stock index, which relies heavily on chip makers that supply AI companies, dropped by 3%.
title: AI-linked stocks fall after tech bosses call for slowdown in ‘reckless’ development

author: Sarah Basford Canales
description:
Indigenous senators have criticised One Nation leader saying the comments showed ‘wilful ignorance’

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

Federal parliamentarians from across the political spectrum have joined in condemning resurfaced comments by Pauline Hanson as “nasty” and “derogatory”, after she labelled Indigenous Australians the “most primitive race on Earth”.

The Indigenous affairs minister, Malarndirri McCarthy, a Yanyuwa and Garrwa woman, describe
title: Pauline Hanson’s comments about Indigenous Australians condemned as ‘nasty’ and ‘derogatory’

author: Libby Brooks
description:
In today’s newsletter: As Labour MPs scramble to realign later today around a bill that could stop donations like this in their tracks, a look at new game-changing donations to a party engulfed in financial scandals

Good morning. Nigel Farage has a confirmed talent for upending the laws of political gravity, and this weekend has been no exception, as he declared himself “humbled” by two donations of £36m each from cryptocurrency tycoons Ben Delo and Christopher Harborne.

I’d shoehorn a joke about buses in here but, honestly, this feels too consequential for that.

Economy | Former chancellor George Osborne said Britain’s economy had “fallen off a cliff” since Brexit – and that rejoining the European Union’s customs union would be the fastest route to recovery.

Technology
title: Monday briefing: What do Reform’s record-setting donations mean for the party – and our politics?

author: Kat Wong
description:
Corruption inquiry turns its investigation to allegations Strathfield councillors may have engaged in blackmail or illegal surveillance

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our new political email, free app or daily news podcast

A Sydney mayor was allegedly threatened, followed and his children were secretly recorded after he refused to honour an agreement to step down, the NSW corruption watchdog has heard.

Former independent Strathfield council mayor Matthew Blackmore has fronted the New South Wales Independ
title: Sydney mayor allegedly threatened and children secretly recorded after he refused to step down, Icac hears

author: Amanda Meade Media correspondent
description:
Alleged victim tells court he froze and was ‘in disbelief’ after broadcaster kissed him on corner of his lips at public event

A prominent athlete froze and was “shocked and embarrassed” when Alan Jones kissed him on the side of his mouth at a public event, the broadcaster’s trial at Sydney’s Downing Centre has heard.

The witness said the kiss on the corner of his lips happened years after Jones sent him a weekly bouquet of flowers after he had complimented the flowers on Jones’s dining table. He said Jones’s driver would drop the flowers at his home every week.

Continue reading...
title: Alan Jones told prominent athlete ‘I would like to be kissing you all night’ after alleged assault, trial hears

author: Australian Associated Press and Benita Kolovos
description:
Coalition says potholes must be fixed ‘as a matter of urgency’ after 71-year-old crashed and died on Western Highway at Trawalla, west of Ballarat, on Sunday

  • Follow our Australia news live blog for latest updates

  • Get our breaking news email, free app or daily news podcast

Emergency services were called to Trawalla, west of Ballarat, shortly before 1pm on Sunday after reports a motorcycle had struck a pothole.

The 71-year-old rider, from Ballarat, died at the scene after reportedly losing control on the Western Highway, near Trawall
title: Motorcyclist’s death reignites debate over potholes on Victoria’s ‘deteriorating’ roads
